input.summary: Make Query.one_of() materialise a one-shot iterator (generator) into a tuple when the query is built, so the per-document `value in items` test and the query hash both use a reusable collection.
input.approach: In `Query.one_of` (tinydb/queries.py:476), before building the test, add: if `items` is an `collections.abc.Iterator` (generators are one; lists, tuples and sets are not), replace it with `tuple(items)`. Both the lambda `value in items` and `freeze(items)` in the hash then use the materialised tuple. Lists and other collections are untouched (FR-QUERY-002). Because the generator is consumed once at construction, the query can be reused across searches and TinyDB instances (FR-QUERY-003). The hash becomes content-based (`('one_of', path, ('a','b'))`) rather than depending on generator object identity (RSK-001), so C2 is satisfied and two one_of queries with the same values correctly share a hash. This needs a stdlib import (`from collections.abc import Iterator`) at the top of queries.py, and a small update to the type hint/docstring if desired (the spec says the docstring stays unchanged, so leave it).

alternatives.option: Make `freeze()` in utils.py convert generators/iterators to tuples
alternatives.why_not: Wider blast radius: freeze is used by every query operation, and the lambda in one_of would still iterate the original, already-consumed generator unless one_of also uses the frozen value. It would also be a larger change than needed.

alternatives.option: Test with `any(value == x for x in items)` or re-create the iterator per document
alternatives.why_not: A generator cannot be re-iterated, so this does not solve it. It would also leave the second search with an empty generator (FR-QUERY-003).

Changes the behaviour of the list and set cases (set membership becomes O(n), the type changes) and conflicts with FR-QUERY-002 'no change for lists'. Restricting to Iterator keeps the change minimal.
Out of scope per spec (Q-003 default (a)); they accept a list or a query, not a generator per their type hints.
Viable and equally small, but Iterator also fixes map/filter/iter() objects, which would otherwise fail silently in the same way; Q-002 leaves this open and the extra coverage is harmless.

files.purpose: Materialise iterator/generator arguments of one_of into a tuple at query-build time.

symbols.name: Query.one_of
symbols.description: If `items` is a collections.abc.Iterator, set `items = tuple(items)` before creating the test lambda and the hash `('one_of', self._path, freeze(items))`. Lists and other collections pass through unchanged.

ac_mapping.test_idea: TinyDB(storage=MemoryStorage) with a,b,a,c; db.search(Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b'])) == [a,b,a].
Build q from a generator; call q on a,b,a,c docs in order; assert True,True,True,False.
Docs a,a,b with a generator yielding a,b; db.count(Query().tag.one_of(gen)) == 3.
Search with list ['a','b'] over a,b,a,c returns [a,b,a].
q = Query().key1.one_of(['value 1','value 2']); q({'key1':'value 1'}) is True, q({'key1':'value 3'}) is False.
Use one list-based query in two db.search calls on a,c docs; both return [a].
Generator-based q searched twice on the same db (a,c docs); both results are [a] (the second call is also checked after clearing the cache with an insert).
Same generator-based q searched on two separate MemoryStorage TinyDBs holding {'tag':'a'}; both return [a].

constraints.how_respected: one_of still goes through Query._generate_test and keeps the hash ('one_of', path, freeze(items)); after materialisation the hash encodes the actual values instead of a generator object identity, so equal-meaning queries share a hash and different ones do not.
Only a stdlib import (collections.abc) is added to queries.py; no import of table.py or database.py.
Uses only the standard library (collections.abc.Iterator, built-in tuple).
Not affected: no change to Table or storage writes.

risks: The spec says 'generator' (TERM-001) but Iterator-based detection also materialises map/filter/iter()/file objects. This is a harmless superset, but it goes beyond the default for Q-002 (a); worth noting for the reviewer.
An infinite generator would now hang at query construction rather than at match time. The only previous behaviour was undefined/partial matches, so this is acceptable.
A generator is consumed at build time, so a caller who later expects to reuse that generator will find it exhausted. This is inherent to generators.
FR-QUERY-003 is ASSUMPTION-ONLY (Q-001 open); the chosen design satisfies it for free, but the spec would still need maintainer confirmation.
The type hint `items: list[Any]` and docstring are left as-is per spec; mypy treats generators as not matching the hint, so only callers' type checkers could complain. Out of scope per spec.
Query.any and Query.all have the same latent issue if given generators; intentionally untouched (Q-003).
